haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, the reservation expires and a sweep job each minute returns the stock to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, the order is REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, and the cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q3: The provider's idempotency key, the order id, makes a repeat of the same request not charge twice. Payment also keeps one payment row per order id, unique.
haiku-low.q4: Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer, and asks Payment to refund the full amount, keyed by order id, retried until done.
haiku-low.q5: The cart is emptied only when the order is CONFIRMED, via the OrderConfirmed event Cart consumes. Every failure leaves the cart exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: Order runs the checkout. Its order record, including status, shows how far each checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment stores the event id, writes the outcome to its outbox, and publishes it to Order as an event.
haiku-low.q8: Payment ignores webhook ids it has already stored. Order acts on an outcome only while the order is STOCK_RESERVED and ignores it otherwise.
haiku-low.q9: Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release the hold. If that request fails, there is no retry; the hold expires after 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory checks whether the hold is still valid, or re-reserves the lines all or nothing if lapsed. Success means fulfil; failure means Order refunds and cancels.
haiku-low.q11: Payment keeps the refund row pending and retries with growing delay, capped at 1 hour, never giving up. It alerts a person after 5 failed attempts.
haiku-low.q12: Order's OrderConfirmed event, written to its outbox when the order is CONFIRMED. The Cart service consumes it and clears the cart.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes (exact expiry time stored on the reservation). If unclaimed, it expires and a minute-by-minute sweep job returns the stock to sale.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing (all or none) and names the short items; Order sets REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, shows the items, requests no payment, and leaves the cart untouched.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) is sent with the provider request, so the provider treats a repeat as the same request and never charges twice. Payment's row is also unique per order id, so a repeated charge call from Order is harmless.
sonnet.q4: Order is set to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is emailed, and Payment is asked to refund the full amount (key = order id). The refund is retried until it succeeds.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when the order is CONFIRMED (Cart clears it on the OrderConfirmed event). Every failure leaves the cart exactly as it was so the customer can try again.
sonnet.q6: Order service runs the checkout and moves it between steps. The record of progress is the order's status, stored in the Order service's database (Order is the only service that changes it).
sonnet.q7: Provider sends a webhook (HTTP call) to Payment. Payment stores the webhook id and writes the outcome to its outbox in one transaction, then publishes the outcome as an event via the broker to Order.
sonnet.q8: Two layers. Payment stores seen webhook ids and ignores a repeated webhook id (replying OK). Order acts on an outcome only while the order is STOCK_RESERVED and ignores it in any other status.
sonnet.q9: Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release the hold, triggered by the declined outcome event from Payment. If the release request fails, there is no retry; the hold expires on its own after 10 minutes.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim. If the hold lapsed, Inventory tries to re-reserve the same lines (all or nothing). If that works, the stock is claimed and the order is CONFIRMED; if not (definite "no"), Order cancels as CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and Payment refunds. Timeouts or errors on claim are not treated as a no; Order repeats the claim until a definite answer.
sonnet.q11: Payment keeps the refund row pending and retries with growing delay (1 minute, doubling, capped at 1 hour), never giving up; after 5 failed attempts it also raises an alert for a person. The pending refund is tracked in Payment (its refund row); Order is not told and stays CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK.
sonnet.q12: Order setting CONFIRMED writes an OrderConfirmed event to its outbox in the same transaction; the Cart service consumes that event and clears the cart. If Cart is down, the broker keeps the event until Cart returns.
